title: Ethics: normative theory and metaethics
audience: a college student in a philosophy degree program, or an adult studying the same material on their own
purpose: Study ethics at the level of a university ethics course: well-being and value, consequentialism, Kantian ethics, contractualism, virtue ethics, moral luck and responsibility, and metaethics (naturalist and non-naturalist realism, error theory, expressivism, constructivism, moral knowledge and the is-ought gap), with careful reconstruction of arguments.

weeks.1: Well-being: hedonism, desire satisfaction and objective lists
weeks.2: Consequentialism: the theory and its variants
weeks.3: Objections to consequentialism: demandingness, rights and integrity
weeks.6: Virtue ethics: character and the good life
weeks.8: Metaethics: the questions and the map of positions
weeks.12: The is-ought gap and moral disagreement

blocks.deliverable: Test three theories of well-being against cases.
Apply the formula of universal law to four maxims.
Compare how contractualism and virtue ethics treat one case.
Week 7 midterm; analyze a moral luck case.
Reconstruct the open question argument and one reply.
Write a three-page essay on moral realism.
Submit the project; take an unseen 120 minute final in week 14.

project: Metaethics paper: write a 2,500-word paper that reconstructs one central argument in metaethics (the argument from disagreement, the argument from queerness, the open question argument or the Frege-Geach problem), evaluates the strongest reply, and defends a conclusion while treating the other side fairly.
completion: finish the project, take the week 7 midterm and week 14 cumulative final, then complete a new cumulative assessment after 1 to 2 weeks. Explain one major idea aloud without notes.
